traps.desc: counted seven jumps instead of six

problems.desc: Part (b): a correct answer says that reaching term seven from term one takes six jumps, not seven, so the step is added one time too many. Full credit for naming the jump count as one less than the term number; partial credit for saying only that the answer is three too big.

traps.desc: counted four jumps from term four to term nine instead of five

problems.desc: Part (c): a correct answer says the rule is stated for term numbers starting at one, so substituting zero names a term that does not exist; the first term is what the rule gives at input one. Full credit for tying the mistake to the stated starting index; no credit for an answer that only reports the right number.

traps.desc: subtracted the two index numbers without adding one

problems.desc: Part (b): a correct answer explains that subtracting the two index numbers counts the gaps between listed terms, and a list has one more term than it has gaps, so one must be added back. Full credit for the gaps-versus-items distinction, illustrated on a short list or in words; partial credit for stating the add-one rule with no reason.

Part (c): a correct answer says starting the index at zero adds one extra term, the value the rule would give one step before the sequence begins, so the total shifts by that value; here that phantom term is negative one, which is why the wrong total is one smaller. Full credit for naming the extra term and its effect on the total.

traps.desc: used the row number as the number of steps
added the step one hundred times instead of ninety-nine

problems.desc: Part (c): a correct sentence says both mistakes come from confusing a count of items with a count of gaps between them: the term number counts terms, while the number of steps added counts gaps, and a run of items always has one more item than gap. Full credit for stating the shared cause rather than describing the two errors separately.
